newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuter German Advertising & Media Digest - May 30.
newsitem.headline: Reuter German Advertising & Media Digest - May 30.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

FRANKFURT - Sports clothing giants Adidas and Reebok say they want to increase their advertising linked to soccer, hitching onto the fan fever surrounding recent German champion league games. (Horizont)

FRANKFURT - Utilities group RWE is investing 10 million marks ($5.9 million) on a new corporate image campaign, focusing on print ads in news and finance magazines and large daily newspapers, which will run for at least a year. Agency Rempen & Partner of Duesseldorf have taken charge of the new campaign. (Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

HAMBURG - Pay-TV station Premiere says it continued its growth trend in May. With over 30,000 new subscriptions, the stations says it surpassed last years's record expansion of 26,000. Premiere says its expects to set further growth records in June with the broadcast of popular films and sports events. (Reuter) *********

WALLDORF - Media group Bertelsmann expects profit for the current year to rise about seven percent compared to last year, despite a drop in turnover. It foresees profit of 255 million marks by the fiscal year-end on June 30, while sales are expected to drop to 3.6 billion marks. Sixty-one percent of this turnover came from Germany, compared with 63 percent last year.
(Kress)

BERLIN - Digital pay TV platform DF1 and pay TV web Premiere are hatching plans to distribute more digital decoders to Teutonic TV households. DF1 will offer new subcribers its complete range of specialised channels along with the D-Box decoder for an introductory price of 49.90 marks ($29) a month. After three months, customers can rent the decoder for $12 a month plus an additional fee for channel packages. (Variety) *********

WALLDORF - The son of Munich media mogul Leo Kirch, Thomas, has taken over private Berlin radio station 100.6, his managing director Georg Gafron says. Thomas Kirch plans to focus programming more heavily on news and will also use the station as an agency to sell programming to third parties. (Kress) ***********************************************
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

HANOVER - Preussag steel and engineering company says it had increased profits and turnover in the first half of 1996-97 fiscal year. The company after-tax profit increased 17.5 percent to 159 million marks and oversees sales boosted 2.1 percent to 11.8 billion marks. (Reuter)

FUSCHL - Austria's Red Bull has led a stampede into the fast-growing energy drinks arena, taking 90 percent of the domestic market and a 30 percent share in Europe, and its success shows no signs of fizzling out. With twice the caffeine of coke, Red Bull is a hit among Europe's clubbers, many of whom have taken to mixing it with vodka to give them pep on the dance floor. (Reuter)

BERLIN - Germans are still passionate tourists despite climbing unemployment and a weak economy, says the German Economic Institute (DIW). German tourists spent about 70 billion marks abroad in 1996, 1.6 billion marks more than in 1995. (Die Welt) *********
BERLIN - Utility group VEAG says it sold more three percent electricity last year but reported lower turnover than in 1995, dropping four percent to 5.7 billion marks. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
WALLDORF - Albert C. Freese, member of the board of Kraft Food International, is leaving the company, Kraft Jacobs Suchard said in Bremen. A successor has not yet been found. (Kress)
Deborah Cole, Berlin Newsroom, 49-30-203-98114
